claims.text: Post-build deep cryogenic treatment improves the dimensional precision of additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components.
Post-build deep cryogenic treatment improves the mechanical integrity of additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components.
Post-build deep cryogenic treatment reduces fabrication-induced defects in additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components.
As-deposited additively manufactured HEAs typically exhibit residual stresses, phase inhomogeneities, and fabrication-induced defects.
DCT can be applied as a post-processing treatment after laser melting deposition of an HEA.
The relevant DCT process consists of extended immersion at deep cryogenic temperature followed by tempering at ambient pressure.
DCT induces lattice distortion in the alloy.
DCT induces a phase transition in laser-additively-manufactured HfNbTaTiZr-based HEA.
DCT forms HCP precipitates near grain boundaries.
DCT refines the alloy microstructure.
DCT redistributes and reduces internal residual stresses.
DCT-induced microstructural changes can correct minor dimensional deviations.
DCT-induced precipitate formation can fill fabrication-induced defects.
DCT-related microstructural refinement improves load distribution and crack arrest.
Relative to as-deposited components, DCT raises tensile strength by approximately 11–25%.
Relative to as-deposited components, DCT improves ductility.
DCT lowers defect density through stress relief and improved phase control.
The intervention may be most effective in HEAs with phase-transformation tendencies, including HfNbTaTiZr-based alloys.
The benefits may not translate to other fabrication methods or alloys lacking comparable phase behavior.
The magnitude of DCT-induced improvement depends on alloy composition, processing parameters, treatment duration, cooling rate, and component geometry.

contradictions.description: The baseline is defined as an untreated as-deposited component with no post-fabrication modification, but the proposed control batch receives surface finishing and tempering. It therefore does not exactly instantiate the stated baseline.
